title: Packaged plugin-set definition
description: machine-bootstrap-contract.md §1.4 / §9. The machine-readable source of truth for bundle membership, host-qualified dependency edges, per-host hook-bearing metadata, and minimum-version floors — shipped as data/plugin-set.json INSIDE the runtime package so a bootstrap invoked from an arbitrary consumer repo can read it. This schema is the STRUCTURAL layer; lib/plugin-set.mjs carries the SEMANTIC layer (edge targets resolve, hard graph is acyclic, bundle closure holds, `full` = all, mandatory membership). Both are required: a structurally perfect definition can still describe an impossible dependency graph.

canonical_marketplace.description: §1.2 — the marketplace SOURCE IDENTITY a registration step is checked against. The step is `satisfied` only on this exact source; a directory/local source is accepted-but-flagged, and a parse failure or absent subcommand is `unknown`, never `satisfied`.

hard_requires.description: §9.1 — behavioral and HOST-QUALIFIED. A hard edge from a retained plugin makes its target non-declinable, and declining it re-runs the closure (§6.2).

soft_requires.description: The contract's §1.4 example shows a bare name list; §9.1 gives soft edges a host scope, and this schema follows §9.1 so hard and soft edges share one shape and one validation path.

hook_bearing.description: §1.4 (as corrected by S8a2 C0) — derived from EFFECTIVE registration: a manifest hook path OR the root hooks/hooks.json default-discovery. So attention is Claude-only, while engineer/orchestrator/founder/designer bear hooks on BOTH hosts. Stage 7 keys off the `codex` value, because Claude trusts plugin hooks by install and exposes no /hooks review flow.

minimum_version.description: §1.4 — the floor, compared PRERELEASE-AWARE with SemVer §11 identifier ranking (numeric identifiers as JS numbers, lossy only above 2^53; beyond the shared semverCompare, whose prerelease tie-break ranks a release above its own prereleases but never identifiers against each other). An unknown installed version with a non-null floor stays `unresolved`, never `installed`. `null` means no floor is claimed.
